relatedSnapshot.title: Name 4 — billed $1,436 for 18 inboxes never created, $144/month still renewing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Bounded context: customer opened with "cancel all subscriptions and billing", then reported he has never had any inboxes or domains but is being charged for both; cancelling his legacy plan lowered the next bill by only $1; Manage Billing shows no subscription list to cancel; the remaining line item is labelled "inbox - inboxes - 18 x 8". He was escalated to a human and has had no answer.

Claim: 18 inboxes were charged at $8/month from 2025-12-03 to date, and $107.77 for 6 pre-warmed domains, but the workspace holds no domains or inboxes, has no outreach account connected, and the purchase record shows 0 of 18 mailbox creations succeeded, so the customer paid for a year of inbox capacity that never existed and has no self-serve control to stop the recurring charge.

Ask bucket: overcharged (money).

Verified money (Stripe, <stripe-id>): $1,554.08 USD collected across 12 paid invoices; nothing refunded; no credit notes; balance 0; no dispute. Of that, $1,436.31 is the 18-inbox charge (first month prorated $140.31 plus nine months at $144.00) and $107.77 is the domain year; $10.00 is the Legacy plan.

Forward exposure: $145.00 due 2026-10-02 and $108.00 due 2026-12-02, then $145.00 monthly, with no in-product cancellation path.

Why there is no cancel path (current code): the Billing page card renders from org mail_domain rows only and shows "No managed domains" when there are none, offering no Cancel control; cancellation runs through cancelManagedDomains, which returns "Domain is not managed by this workspace" when no mail_domain row exists. Cancelling the named plan product cancels only that product, which is the $1 reduction the customer saw. Repository HEAD read: f0228bab1e57b287a17a66e2e042abc3de8191dd.

Discretion: needs-human. All three systems of record agree the add-ons are live and paid, so this is not a sync fault; the divergence is between what was paid for and what exists in the workspace. No prior approval or promise exists in the conversation or the request, so the amount decision is a person's.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise):

1. Cancel the live Inbox add-on ($8 x 18) and the Domain add-on on billing account 7de4ed09.../Stripe subscription <stripe-id> before the 2026-10-02 renewal, so the October and December charges cannot land.
2. Decide the refund: $1,436.31 for inbox capacity never created plus an amount for the domain year the customer never had visible, out of $1,554.08 collected. No refund or credit has been issued.
3. Tell the customer, because he has had no answer since Fin AI escalated him on 2026-09-29.

Unverified on this ticket: the customer's purchase intent at signup; whether the December 2025 order flow code matches today's HEAD, so no failing function is attributed; the provider-side cancellation record for these six domains (the cancellation log table starts 2026-08-01 and holds no row for them).

relatedSnapshot.title: Overcharged for inbox and domain seats — billed 24 inbox seats while 12 live on the workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation. Contact Name 14, <email>, workspace "Company Seven" (the billing URL in the conversation pins it: <url:app.acquisity.ai>). She opened with "i have a billing question", attached a screenshot of the Billing page and asked "why does my billing say i owe $96/month for 12 total inboxes but then it says below $24/month x 4 domains," then "then why am i getting billed double that per month", then "speak to a human". Fin AI twice explained it away as the same cost shown two ways; she did not accept that. She then sent a second screenshot of the page's "Invoices & payment history" table and asked "checking the Payment history, there were other charges. Where is this coming from?" No requested remedy stated, only that the monthly amount looks wrong.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the Billing page is not double counting. The $96/month "Total Inboxes" line and the "$24/month x 4 domains" rows are the same 12 inboxes recomputed, which is why they agree. The real divergence is that her billing account carries 24 inbox seats and 8 domain seats while the workspace holds 12 live inboxes on 4 active domains.

* Billed: 18 inbox seats ($24 + $24 + $96 = $144.00/month) + 6 inbox seats (6 x $8.00 = $48.00/month) = $192.00/month; and 6 + 2 = 8 domain seats = $144.00/year; plus a $1.00/month legacy plan.
* Live: 4 active domains with 3 prewarmed inboxes each = 12 inboxes.
* Excess: 12 inbox seats ($96.00/month) and 4 domain seats ($72.00/year). The excess inbox seats are exactly the $96/month she pointed at.

Her second screenshot answers "where is this coming from". Every row is a real paid invoice on this billing account, and the two recurring lines are the two subscriptions renewing on different days of the month: $144.00 on the 24th (the 18-seat subscription) and $48.00 on the 19th (the older 6-seat legacy subscription). The $23.75 and $10.00 rows are one-off credit purchases, not subscriptions, so they are not part of the recurring cost. Nothing in the history is a duplicate, a refund, a credit note, or a failed payment.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise): reconcile the live add-on seats on the billing account against the resources genuinely in the workspace, end the excess inbox and domain line items so the recurring charge stops, and decide the refund of the overcollected amount against the uncapped charge history. She has no self-serve path to remove the excess seats.

Open human decisions: the customer has not yet said whether she wants money back or a credit, and the suspended <domain> domain's 3 inboxes are excluded from the Billing page but not obviously excluded from billing.

#### What are you trying to achieve?

We are helping a client, Name 18 (Company Four AI Agency, <email>), understand his recent charges. He is a serious escalation, and in his own words the June 10 and July 10 charges are what remain in question for him. He wants to be sure he is not being over-billed before he updates his card, so we are trying to give him a clear, itemized explanation of both charges to put his mind at ease.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

We reviewed his invoice history ourselves first. The June 10 charge of $252 reconciles cleanly on our end as 6 domains at $18 annual ($108) plus 18 inboxes at $8 ($144). The old $144 Company Eight inbox subscription is already confirmed cancelled, so that one is settled. But Name 19 cannot see that line-item detail from his side, which is why both June 10 and July 10 remain open questions for him.

#### What is happening instead?

The July 10 charge of $264 ("Inbox - Inboxes") is coming in higher than we would expect. Based on his 18 inboxes at $8 we would have anticipated around $144, so there is roughly $120 we cannot account for. We want to understand it correctly before explaining it back to Name 19, so we do not give him the wrong information.

#### What is the expected outcome?

We would appreciate your help with an itemized breakdown of both charges Name 19 flagged: the June 10 $252 and the July 10 $264. For July 10 specifically, it would help to understand whether the $264 reflects a larger inbox count or something else, and whether any domain amount is included (domains were billed annually on June 10, so we would not expect them here). If anything looks off, we will take it from there with the client. For context, both July charges currently show Failed, so nothing has actually been taken yet.

relatedSnapshot.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 22

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Company Five

#### Screenshot

 <image> 

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Two things: (1) determine whether his inboxes and domains not showing is a sync issue or an actual cancellation, since his billing shows a September charge but no inboxes or domains display, and (2) audit his entire billing history for overcharges, including a clear record of how many inboxes and domains he had at each point over time, because he also cancelled a number of them.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

On a call we exited the onboarding state (triggered by inactivity since March) and confirmed his Acquisity plan at $129 per month is correct. Checked his Email accounts section and the cold email agent, where the 18 inboxes flickered in and out on reload.

#### What is happening instead?

His billing shows a $144 charge scheduled for Sep 7, which lines up with 6 domains and 18 inboxes, but his Email accounts section shows none. The inboxes appearing and disappearing on reload points to a sync issue rather than a cancellation. The client also says he cancelled a number of inboxes over the past months and believes he was overcharged during his inactive period since March, when billing rose from $192 to $216.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Confirmation of whether this is a sync issue or a real cancellation, his inboxes and domains displaying correctly, and a full billing history audit showing how many inboxes and domains he held at each point versus what he was charged, with any overcharge identified and a credit or refund processed.
